# Flightbroom settings reference

<!-- GENERATED by `flb settings reference` from crates/flb-presets/data/tags.json and crates/flb-protocol/data/descriptions.json. Do not edit by hand; regenerate with: cargo run -p flb-cli -- settings reference > docs/ai/settings-reference.md -->

Every Camera Raw (`crs:`) setting Flightbroom knows, grouped as in the tag registry. Use the **Tag** name with `flb edit` commands (`set_param`, `adjust_param`, `reset_param`) and the **group** name with `reset_group` and `apply_preset` filters. See [README.md](README.md) for how to drive Flightbroom.

How to read the tables:
- **Range / Default**: best-known values from the registry. Most are not yet verified against Lightroom. Numbers outside the range are clamped, and the clamping is reported. An empty default means the value depends on the image (e.g. As Shot white balance) or the tag has no single default.
- A setting that is absent from a sidecar means "untouched": its default applies. `reset_param` removes a setting.
- **Status** is Flightbroom's rendering support: *rendered (approx.)* = the engine renders it with a model not yet fitted to Lightroom; *planned* = stored and round-tripped, not rendered yet; *image-specific* = depends on one photo (crop, auto settings), presets should rarely carry it; *metadata* = describes the file, not the look; *unsupported* = recognised AI/cloud feature, kept but never rendered.
- Descriptions follow Adobe's help (digested in `docs/adobe-docs/`). Where Adobe does not document something, the description says so.

## Preset metadata (`metadata`)

Describes the preset or sidecar itself (name, group, UUID, Amount-slider support). Not an edit; never changes how the photo looks.

| Tag | Control | Kind | Range | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Name` | Preset name | text |  |  | metadata | Display name of the preset (an XMP language alternative or plain text). |
| `Group` | Preset group | text |  |  | metadata | The group (folder) the preset is listed under. |
| `Cluster` | Preset cluster | text |  |  | metadata | Adobe preset grouping key used alongside Group. |
| `ShortName` | Short name | text |  |  | metadata | Short display name of the preset. |
| `SortName` | Sort name | text |  |  | metadata | Name used to sort the preset in lists. |
| `Description` | Preset description | text |  |  | metadata | Free-text description of the preset. |
| `Copyright` | Copyright | text |  |  | metadata | Copyright notice of the preset. |
| `ContactInfo` | Contact info | text |  |  | metadata | Contact information of the preset author. |
| `UUID` | Preset UUID | text |  |  | metadata | Unique identifier of the preset. |
| `PresetType` | Preset type | text |  |  | metadata | Kind of preset, e.g. Normal. Its presence marks an XMP file as a preset rather than a sidecar. |
| `CameraModelRestriction` | Camera restriction | text |  |  | metadata | Camera model the preset is restricted to (e.g. for camera-specific profiles). |
| `SupportsAmount` | Supports Amount slider | bool | true / false |  | metadata | True when the preset may be applied with the Amount slider. When False, Lightroom greys the slider out. |
| `SupportsAmount2` | Supports Amount slider (v2) | bool | true / false |  | metadata | Newer form of SupportsAmount. |
| `SupportsColor` | Supports colour photos | bool | true / false |  | metadata | Whether the preset is meant for colour photos. |
| `SupportsMonochrome` | Supports monochrome photos | bool | true / false |  | metadata | Whether the preset is meant for monochrome photos. |
| `SupportsHighDynamicRange` | Supports HDR | bool | true / false |  | metadata | Whether the preset supports HDR edits. |
| `SupportsNormalDynamicRange` | Supports SDR | bool | true / false |  | metadata | Whether the preset supports standard dynamic range edits. |
| `SupportsSceneReferred` | Supports scene-referred | bool | true / false |  | metadata | Whether the preset supports scene-referred (raw-like) images. |
| `SupportsOutputReferred` | Supports output-referred | bool | true / false |  | metadata | Whether the preset supports output-referred (JPEG/TIFF-like) images. |
| `HasSettings` | Has settings | bool | true / false |  | metadata | Whether the file carries develop settings. |
| `RequiresRGBTables` | Requires RGB tables | bool | true / false |  | metadata | Whether the preset needs embedded RGB lookup tables (Table_* entries). |
| `RawFileName` | Raw file name | text |  |  | metadata | File name of the raw the sidecar belongs to. |

<a id="process"></a>

## Process version (`process`)

The Camera Raw processing technology. It decides which tone controls exist (PV2012 and later: Exposure2012..Blacks2012; PV2010/2003: the legacy controls). Updating it can change the look significantly.

| Tag | Control | Kind | Range | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Version` | Writer version | text |  |  | metadata | Version of the Camera Raw engine that wrote the file. |
| `CompatibleVersion` | Compatible version | text |  |  | metadata | Oldest Camera Raw version that can read the settings. |
| `ProcessVersion` | Process version | text |  |  | metadata | Camera Raw process version as a version string (e.g. "15.4"). It decides which tone controls apply; Adobe's help does not list the numeric identifiers. |
| `AlreadyApplied` | Already applied | bool | true / false |  | metadata | Marks settings that were already baked into the pixels (e.g. a rendered file). |

## Profile (`profile`)

The colour and tone foundation (Adobe Color, Adobe Monochrome, Camera Matching, creative profiles). Applying a profile does not change any slider values.

| Tag | Control | Kind | Range | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CameraProfile` | Profile | text |  |  | planned | Name of the camera profile, e.g. "Adobe Color" (the default for raw photos), "Adobe Monochrome", "Adobe Landscape", "Adobe Portrait", "Adobe Neutral", "Adobe Vivid", or a Camera Matching profile. Applying a profile does not change slider values. |
| `CameraProfileDigest` | Profile digest | text |  |  | planned | Checksum identifying the exact camera profile. |
| `Look` | Look (creative profile) | struct |  |  | planned | Creative profile (Artistic, B&W, Modern, Vintage, ...) stored as a structure with its name, parameters and Amount. |
| `RGBTable` | RGB table | text |  |  | planned | Reference to an embedded RGB lookup table used by a profile or look. |
| `LookTable` | Look table | text |  |  | planned | Reference to an embedded look table used by a profile. |
| `OverrideLookVignette` | Override look vignette | bool | true / false |  | planned | Whether the photo's own vignette settings override the one built into a creative profile. |

<a id="white-balance"></a>

## Basic: White balance (`white_balance`)

White balance preset, Temp and Tint. Raw files use a Kelvin Temp scale; JPEG/TIFF use an approximate -100..100 scale (the Incremental* tags).

| Tag | Control | Kind | Range | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `WhiteBalance` | White balance preset | enum |  |  | rendered (approx.) | "As Shot" (the camera's setting), "Auto" (computed from the image), or for raw/DNG "Daylight", "Cloudy", "Shade", "Tungsten", "Fluorescent", "Flash"; "Custom" when Temp/Tint were set by hand. Temperature and Tint only take effect when this is not "As Shot" (Flightbroom's edit commands switch it to "Custom" when you set Temp or Tint). |
| `Temperature` | Temp | number | 2000 to 50000 |  | rendered (approx.) | *Units: K.* Colour temperature in Kelvin for raw files: lower values make the photo cooler (bluer), higher values warmer (more yellow). Example: 3200 K suits tungsten light. Adobe documents 2000-50000 K (newer versions go down to 1500 K). No default: As Shot depends on the camera's recorded white balance. |
| `Tint` | Tint | number | -150 to 150 |  | rendered (approx.) | Green/magenta balance: negative adds green, positive adds magenta. 0 = neutral relative to the white balance preset. |
| `IncrementalTemperature` | Temp (non-raw) | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | Temp for JPEG/TIFF/PSD files, on an approximate -100..100 scale instead of Kelvin: negative cooler, positive warmer. |
| `IncrementalTint` | Tint (non-raw) | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | Tint for JPEG/TIFF/PSD files on a -100..100 scale: negative greener, positive more magenta. |

<a id="tone"></a>

## Basic: Tone (`tone`)

Global tone controls for process version 2012 and later: Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks.

| Tag | Control | Kind | Range | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Exposure2012` | Exposure | number | -5 to 5 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | *Units: stops.* Overall image brightness, in stops: +1.00 is similar to opening the aperture one stop, -1.00 to closing it one stop. |
| `Contrast2012` | Contrast | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Mainly affects midtones. Increasing it makes middle-to-dark areas darker and middle-to-light areas lighter; decreasing it flattens the image. |
| `Highlights2012` | Highlights | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Adjusts bright areas. Negative darkens highlights and recovers blown-out detail; positive brightens them while minimising clipping. |
| `Shadows2012` | Shadows | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Adjusts dark areas. Negative darkens shadows while minimising clipping; positive brightens them and recovers shadow detail. |
| `Whites2012` | Whites | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Adjusts white clipping. Negative reduces clipping in highlights; positive increases it (sometimes desirable for specular highlights). |
| `Blacks2012` | Blacks | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Adjusts black clipping. Negative maps more shadows to pure black (deeper blacks); positive reduces shadow clipping (lifts the black point). |
| `AutoTone` | Auto tone | bool | true / false | false | image-specific | True when the tone sliders were set by Auto, which maximises the tonal scale and minimises clipping for that particular image. |

<a id="tone-legacy"></a>

## Basic: Tone (legacy PV2010/PV2003) (`tone_legacy`)

Tone controls of the old process versions. Only meaningful for photos still on PV2010/PV2003. For current edits use the 'tone' and 'presence' groups (Exposure2012, Contrast2012, Clarity2012, ...).

| Tag | Control | Kind | Range | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Exposure` | Exposure (legacy) | number | -4 to 4 | 0 | planned | *Units: stops.* PV2010/PV2003 Exposure, in stops. For current process versions use Exposure2012. |
| `Brightness` | Brightness (legacy) | number | -150 to 150 | 50 | planned | PV2010/PV2003 Brightness: mainly midtones; moving right compresses highlights and expands shadows. No PV2012 equivalent; use Exposure2012 and the tone curve. |
| `Contrast` | Contrast (legacy) | number | -50 to 100 | 25 | planned | PV2010/PV2003 Contrast, mainly affecting midtones. For current process versions use Contrast2012. |
| `Shadows` | Blacks (legacy) | number | 0 to 100 | 5 | planned | The PV2010/PV2003 Blacks slider: which image values map to black, with the greatest effect in the shadows. For current process versions use Blacks2012 (and Shadows2012 for shadow brightness). |
| `HighlightRecovery` | Recovery (legacy) | number | 0 to 100 | 0 | planned | PV2010/PV2003 Recovery: reduces extreme highlights and can recover detail when one or two channels are clipped. For current process versions use Highlights2012. |
| `FillLight` | Fill Light (legacy) | number | 0 to 100 | 0 | planned | PV2010/PV2003 Fill Light: lightens shadows while keeping blacks; may reveal noise. For current process versions use Shadows2012. |
| `Clarity` | Clarity (legacy) | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | PV2010 Clarity. For current process versions use Clarity2012. |

<a id="presence"></a>

## Basic: Presence (`presence`)

Texture, Clarity, Dehaze, Vibrance and Saturation.

| Tag | Control | Kind | Range | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Texture` | Texture | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | Smooths (negative) or accentuates (positive) textured detail without changing colour or tonality. |
| `Clarity2012` | Clarity | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | Local contrast, like a large-radius unsharp mask that acts mostly on midtones. Positive values add depth and punch; too much draws light or dark rims (halos) along strong edges. Negative values soften local contrast. |
| `Dehaze` | Dehaze | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | Positive removes haze; negative adds haze for a softer, misty look. |
| `Vibrance` | Vibrance | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Raises the saturation of lower-saturated colours with less effect on already saturated ones, minimising clipping and keeping skin tones from becoming oversaturated. |
| `Saturation` | Saturation | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Saturation of all colours equally: -100 is monochrome, +100 doubles the saturation. |

<a id="tone-curve"></a>

## Tone Curve (`tone_curve`)

Parametric curve (four region sliders and three split points) and point curves (combined RGB plus Red, Green and Blue channels). Input on the horizontal axis, output on the vertical; a straight 45-degree line means no change.

| Tag | Control | Kind | Range | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ToneCurveName2012` | Point curve preset | text |  |  | planned | Name of the point curve preset: "Linear", "Medium Contrast", "Strong Contrast", or "Custom". The preset is reflected in the point curve, not in the region sliders. |
| `ToneCurveName` | Point curve preset (legacy) | text |  |  | planned | PV2010/PV2003 point curve preset name. |
| `ToneCurvePV2012` | Point curve (RGB) | curve | points 0-255 |  | rendered (approx.) | *Units: 0-255 points.* Combined RGB point curve as a list of "input, output" points on a 0-255 scale (e.g. [[0,0],[64,56],[192,200],[255,255]] for gentle contrast). [[0,0],[255,255]] is the straight 45-degree line: no change. Raising the first point's output lifts (fades) the blacks; lowering the last point's output dims the whites. |
| `ToneCurvePV2012Red` | Point curve (Red) | curve | points 0-255 |  | rendered (approx.) | *Units: 0-255 points.* Red-channel point curve, same format as ToneCurvePV2012. Raising it adds red, lowering it adds cyan, in the tones the points cover. |
| `ToneCurvePV2012Green` | Point curve (Green) | curve | points 0-255 |  | rendered (approx.) | *Units: 0-255 points.* Green-channel point curve, same format as ToneCurvePV2012. Raising it adds green, lowering it adds magenta, in the tones the points cover. |
| `ToneCurvePV2012Blue` | Point curve (Blue) | curve | points 0-255 |  | rendered (approx.) | *Units: 0-255 points.* Blue-channel point curve, same format as ToneCurvePV2012. Raising it adds blue, lowering it adds yellow, in the tones the points cover. |
| `ToneCurve` | Point curve (legacy) | curve | points 0-255 |  | planned | *Units: 0-255 points.* PV2010/PV2003 point curve. For current process versions use ToneCurvePV2012. |
| `ParametricShadows` | Curve: Shadows | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Parametric curve region slider for the darkest end of the tonal range. Negative darkens, positive lightens. |
| `ParametricDarks` | Curve: Darks | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Parametric curve region slider for the darker middle region. Negative darkens, positive lightens. |
| `ParametricLights` | Curve: Lights | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Parametric curve region slider for the lighter middle region. Negative darkens, positive lightens. |
| `ParametricHighlights` | Curve: Highlights | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Parametric curve region slider for the brightest end of the tonal range. Negative darkens, positive lightens. |
| `ParametricShadowSplit` | Curve: Shadows/Darks split | number | 10 to 70 | 25 | rendered (approx.) | Position of the boundary between the Shadows and Darks regions, as a percentage of the tonal range. |
| `ParametricMidtoneSplit` | Curve: Darks/Lights split | number | 20 to 80 | 50 | rendered (approx.) | Position of the boundary between the Darks and Lights regions, as a percentage of the tonal range. |
| `ParametricHighlightSplit` | Curve: Lights/Highlights split | number | 30 to 90 | 75 | rendered (approx.) | Position of the boundary between the Lights and Highlights regions, as a percentage of the tonal range. |

## Color Mixer: HSL (`hsl`)

Hue, Saturation and Luminance per colour band (Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Aqua, Blue, Purple, Magenta). Each slider affects all similar colours in the photo.

| Tag | Control | Kind | Range | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HueAdjustmentRed` | Hue: Red | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Shifts the hue of red colours in the photo (changes the colour itself, e.g. a blue sky towards cyan or purple). 0 = unchanged. |
| `SaturationAdjustmentRed` | Saturation: Red | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Vividness or purity of red colours. Negative mutes them, positive intensifies them. 0 = unchanged. |
| `LuminanceAdjustmentRed` | Luminance: Red | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Brightness of red colours. Negative darkens them, positive lightens them. 0 = unchanged. |
| `HueAdjustmentOrange` | Hue: Orange | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Shifts the hue of orange colours in the photo (changes the colour itself, e.g. a blue sky towards cyan or purple). 0 = unchanged. |

| `LuminanceAdjustmentOrange` | Luminance: Orange | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Brightness of orange colours. Negative darkens them, positive lightens them. 0 = unchanged. |

<a id="bw-mixer"></a>

## Black & White (`bw_mixer`)

Black & white treatment and the B&W Mix: how light or dark each colour band becomes in grey.

| Tag | Control | Kind | Range | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GrayMixerRed` | B&W Mix: Red | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | In a black & white conversion, how light or dark red areas of the original become in grey. Negative darkens, positive lightens. Only has an effect when ConvertToGrayscale is True. |
| `GrayMixerOrange` | B&W Mix: Orange | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | In a black & white conversion, how light or dark orange areas of the original become in grey. Negative darkens, positive lightens. Only has an effect when ConvertToGrayscale is True. |
| `GrayMixerYellow` | B&W Mix: Yellow | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | In a black & white conversion, how light or dark yellow areas of the original become in grey. Negative darkens, positive lightens. Only has an effect when ConvertToGrayscale is True. |
| `GrayMixerGreen` | B&W Mix: Green | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | In a black & white conversion, how light or dark green areas of the original become in grey. Negative darkens, positive lightens. Only has an effect when ConvertToGrayscale is True. |
| `GrayMixerAqua` | B&W Mix: Aqua | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | In a black & white conversion, how light or dark aqua areas of the original become in grey. Negative darkens, positive lightens. Only has an effect when ConvertToGrayscale is True. |
| `GrayMixerBlue` | B&W Mix: Blue | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | In a black & white conversion, how light or dark blue areas of the original become in grey. Negative darkens, positive lightens. Only has an effect when ConvertToGrayscale is True. |
| `GrayMixerPurple` | B&W Mix: Purple | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | In a black & white conversion, how light or dark purple areas of the original become in grey. Negative darkens, positive lightens. Only has an effect when ConvertToGrayscale is True. |
| `GrayMixerMagenta` | B&W Mix: Magenta | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | In a black & white conversion, how light or dark magenta areas of the original become in grey. Negative darkens, positive lightens. Only has an effect when ConvertToGrayscale is True. |
| `ConvertToGrayscale` | Treatment: Black & White | bool | true / false | false | planned | True converts the photo to black & white (the B&W Mix sliders then set each colour's grey tone); False keeps colour. |
| `AutoGrayscaleMix` | Auto B&W mix | bool | true / false | false | image-specific | True when the B&W Mix was set by Auto, which maximises the distribution of grey tones for that image. |

Targeted changes to one sampled colour (up to eight swatches): Hue/Saturation/Luminance Shift, Variance and Range.

<a id="color-grading"></a>

## Color Grading (`color_grading`)

Colour wheels for Shadows, Midtones, Highlights and Global (hue, saturation, luminance each), plus Blending. Balance is stored in SplitToningBalance.

| Tag | Control | Kind | Range | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ColorGradeShadowHue` | Grading: Shadows hue | number | 0 to 359 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | *Units: degrees.* Hue of the tint added to shadows, as an angle on the colour wheel (0-359). Has no effect while ColorGradeShadowSat is 0. |
| `ColorGradeShadowSat` | Grading: Shadows saturation | number | 0 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Strength of the shadows tint: 0 = none, 100 = strongest. |
| `ColorGradeMidtoneHue` | Grading: Midtones hue | number | 0 to 359 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | *Units: degrees.* Hue of the tint added to midtones (0-359 on the colour wheel). Has no effect while ColorGradeMidtoneSat is 0. |
| `ColorGradeMidtoneSat` | Grading: Midtones saturation | number | 0 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Strength of the midtones tint: 0 = none, 100 = strongest. |
| `ColorGradeHighlightHue` | Grading: Highlights hue | number | 0 to 359 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | *Units: degrees.* Hue of the tint added to highlights (0-359 on the colour wheel). Has no effect while ColorGradeHighlightSat is 0. |
| `ColorGradeHighlightSat` | Grading: Highlights saturation | number | 0 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Strength of the highlights tint: 0 = none, 100 = strongest. |
| `ColorGradeGlobalHue` | Grading: Global hue | number | 0 to 359 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | *Units: degrees.* Hue of a tint applied to the whole image (0-359), without changing the shadows/midtones/highlights wheels. Has no effect while ColorGradeGlobalSat is 0. |
| `ColorGradeGlobalSat` | Grading: Global saturation | number | 0 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Strength of the global tint: 0 = none, 100 = strongest. |
| `ColorGradeShadowLum` | Grading: Shadows luminance | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Brightness of the shadows: negative darkens, positive lightens. |
| `ColorGradeHighlightLum` | Grading: Highlights luminance | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Brightness of the highlights: negative darkens, positive lightens. |
| `ColorGradeMidtoneLum` | Grading: Midtones luminance | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Brightness of the midtones: negative darkens, positive lightens. |
| `ColorGradeGlobalLum` | Grading: Global luminance | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Overall brightness change from the global wheel: negative darkens, positive lightens. |
| `ColorGradeBlending` | Grading: Blending | number | 0 to 100 | 50 | rendered (approx.) | Amount of overlap (smoothness of the transition) between the shadows, midtones and highlights wheels. Higher values maximise the overlap. |

The pre-2020 Split Toning controls. Camera Raw reuses SplitToningBalance as the Color Grading Balance slider.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SplitToningShadowHue` | Split toning: Shadows hue | number | 0 to 359 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | *Units: degrees.* Legacy split-toning shadow hue (0-359). Current Lightroom shows it as the Color Grading shadows wheel. |
| `SplitToningHighlightHue` | Split toning: Highlights hue | number | 0 to 359 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | *Units: degrees.* Legacy split-toning highlight hue (0-359). Current Lightroom shows it as the Color Grading highlights wheel. |
| `SplitToningShadowSaturation` | Split toning: Shadows saturation | number | 0 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Legacy split-toning shadow tint strength (0-100). |
| `SplitToningHighlightSaturation` | Split toning: Highlights saturation | number | 0 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Legacy split-toning highlight tint strength (0-100). |
| `SplitToningBalance` | Grading: Balance | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | rendered (approx.) | Color Grading (and legacy split toning) Balance: positive values increase the influence of the highlight controls, negative values the influence of the shadow controls. |

<a id="detail"></a>

## Detail (`detail`)

Sharpening (Amount, Radius, Detail, Masking) and manual noise reduction (luminance and colour). Judge these at 100% zoom or more.

| Tag | Control | Kind | Range | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Sharpness` | Sharpening: Amount | number | 0 to 150 | 40 | planned | Edge definition: increases contrast between pixels that differ from their neighbours. 0 turns sharpening off. Part of the camera default applied at import. |
| `SharpenRadius` | Sharpening: Radius | number | 0.5 to 3 | 1 | planned | *Units: px.* Size of the details that sharpening is applied to: lower for very fine detail; too large looks unnatural. |
| `SharpenDetail` | Sharpening: Detail | number | 0 to 100 | 25 | planned | Which detail gets sharpened. At low values only clear edges are sharpened; at high values fine texture (skin, fabric, foliage) is sharpened too. |
| `SharpenEdgeMasking` | Sharpening: Masking | number | 0 to 100 | 0 | planned | Edge mask: 0 sharpens everything equally; 100 restricts sharpening mostly to the areas near the strongest edges. |
| `LuminanceSmoothing` | Noise reduction: Luminance | number | 0 to 100 | 0 | planned | Reduces luminance (brightness) noise. 0 = off. |
| `LuminanceNoiseReductionDetail` | Noise reduction: Detail | number | 0 to 100 | 50 | planned | Luminance noise threshold. Higher preserves more detail but may leave more noise; lower gives cleaner results but may remove some detail. |
| `LuminanceNoiseReductionContrast` | Noise reduction: Contrast | number | 0 to 100 | 0 | planned | Higher preserves contrast but may produce noisy blotches or mottling; lower gives smoother results with less contrast. |
| `ColorNoiseReduction` | Color noise reduction | number | 0 to 100 | 25 | planned | Reduces colour noise (coloured speckles). 0 = off. |
| `ColorNoiseReductionDetail` | Color noise reduction: Detail | number | 0 to 100 | 50 | planned | Colour noise threshold. Higher protects thin, detailed colour edges but may leave colour speckling; lower removes speckles but may cause colour bleeding. |
| `ColorNoiseReductionSmoothness` | Color noise reduction: Smoothness | number | 0 to 100 | 50 | planned | Smoothness sub-slider of colour noise reduction. Adobe's help names it without describing it further. |

<a id="lens"></a>

## Lens Corrections (`lens`)

Lens profile corrections, chromatic-aberration removal, defringing and lens vignetting.

| Tag | Control | Kind | Range | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LensProfileEnable` | Enable profile corrections | bool | true / false | false | planned | True applies the lens profile matched from the camera and lens metadata (distortion and vignetting correction). |
| `AutoLateralCA` | Remove chromatic aberration | bool | true / false | false | planned | True automatically corrects blue-yellow and red-green lateral colour fringes. |
| `LensProfileSetup` | Lens profile setup | text |  |  | planned | How the lens profile was chosen (e.g. automatic or custom). |
| `LensProfileName` | Lens profile | text |  |  | planned | Name of the lens profile in use. |
| `LensProfileFilename` | Lens profile file | text |  |  | planned | File name of the lens profile (.lcp). |
| `LensProfileDigest` | Lens profile digest | text |  |  | planned | Checksum identifying the exact lens profile. |
| `LensProfileDistortionScale` | Profile: Distortion | number | 0 to 200 | 100 | planned | *Units: %.* How much of the profile's distortion correction is applied: 100 = 100% of the profile, above 100 corrects more, below 100 less. |
| `LensProfileVignettingScale` | Profile: Vignetting | number | 0 to 200 | 100 | planned | *Units: %.* How much of the profile's vignetting correction is applied: 100 = 100% of the profile, above 100 corrects more, below 100 less. |
| `LensProfileChromaticAberrationScale` | Profile: Chromatic aberration | number | 0 to 200 | 100 | planned | *Units: %.* Scale of the profile's chromatic-aberration correction, 100 = as profiled. Not described in Adobe's help. |
| `LensManualDistortionAmount` | Manual: Distortion | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | Manual distortion correction: positive corrects barrel distortion, negative corrects pincushion distortion. |
| `VignetteAmount` | Lens vignetting: Amount | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | Manual lens vignetting correction: positive lightens the corners, negative darkens them. See PostCropVignetteAmount for a creative vignette relative to the crop. |
| `VignetteMidpoint` | Lens vignetting: Midpoint | number | 0 to 100 | 50 | planned | Midpoint of the manual lens vignetting correction. Adobe's help names it without further detail. |
| `DefringePurpleAmount` | Defringe: Purple amount | number | 0 to 20 | 0 | planned | Strength of purple fringe removal along high-contrast edges (handles longitudinal chromatic aberration). 0 = off. |
| `DefringeGreenAmount` | Defringe: Green amount | number | 0 to 20 | 0 | planned | Strength of green fringe removal along high-contrast edges. 0 = off. |
| `DefringePurpleHueLo` | Defringe: Purple hue (low) | number | 0 to 100 |  | planned | Lower end of the hue range treated as purple fringing. The two ends stay at least 10 units apart. |
| `DefringeGreenHueLo` | Defringe: Green hue (low) | number | 0 to 100 |  | planned | Lower end of the hue range treated as green fringing. The default range is narrow to protect green/yellow subjects such as foliage. |
| `DefringePurpleHueHi` | Defringe: Purple hue (high) | number | 0 to 100 |  | planned | Upper end of the hue range treated as purple fringing. The two ends stay at least 10 units apart. |
| `DefringeGreenHueHi` | Defringe: Green hue (high) | number | 0 to 100 |  | planned | Upper end of the hue range treated as green fringing. The default range is narrow to protect green/yellow subjects such as foliage. |

<a id="effects"></a>

## Effects (`effects`)

Post-crop vignette (styles, Amount, Midpoint, Roundness, Feather, Highlights) and film grain (Amount, Size, Roughness).

| Tag | Control | Kind | Range | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PostCropVignetteAmount` | Vignette: Amount | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | Creative vignette relative to the crop: negative darkens the corners, positive lightens them. 0 = off. |
| `PostCropVignetteMidpoint` | Vignette: Midpoint | number | 0 to 100 | 50 | planned | Lower values apply the Amount to a larger area away from the corners; higher values keep it closer to the corners. |
| `PostCropVignetteFeather` | Vignette: Feather | number | 0 to 100 | 50 | planned | Softness of the vignette edge: lower values soften less (harder edge). |
| `PostCropVignetteRoundness` | Vignette: Roundness | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | Positive makes the vignette more circular, negative more oval. |
| `PostCropVignetteHighlightContrast` | Vignette: Highlights | number | 0 to 100 | 0 | planned | How much highlight contrast is preserved when Amount is negative (Highlight Priority and Color Priority styles only); suits photos with small highlights such as candles and lamps. |
| `PostCropVignetteStyle` | Vignette: Style | enum | 1 to 3 | 1 | planned | Highlight Priority (protects highlight contrast, may shift colours in darkened areas), Color Priority (preserves hues, may lose detail in bright highlights) or Paint Overlay (blends with black or white; can look flat). Stored as a number; the 1 = Highlight Priority, 2 = Color Priority, 3 = Paint Overlay encoding is Camera Raw's XMP convention, not stated in Adobe's help. |
| `GrainAmount` | Grain: Amount | number | 0 to 100 | 0 | planned | Strength of simulated film grain. 0 = off. |
| `GrainSize` | Grain: Size | number | 0 to 100 | 25 | planned | Grain particle size. At 25 or more Adobe adds blue to work better with noise reduction, and such sizes can cause some image blurring. |
| `GrainFrequency` | Grain: Roughness | number | 0 to 100 | 50 | planned | Grain regularity: lower is more uniform, higher more uneven. Together with Size it sets the grain's character. |
| `GrainSeed` | Grain seed | number | any number |  | image-specific | Random seed of the grain pattern, specific to one image. |

<a id="calibration"></a>

## Calibration (`calibration`)

Shadows tint and the red, green and blue primary hue/saturation adjustments to the camera's default colour rendering.

| Tag | Control | Kind | Range | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ShadowTint` | Calibration: Shadows | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | Corrects a green or magenta tint in the shadow areas of the photo. |
| `RedHue` | Calibration: Red primary hue | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | Shifts the hue of the camera's red primary; negative is roughly counterclockwise on the colour wheel. Adjust hue first, then saturation. |
| `RedSaturation` | Calibration: Red primary saturation | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | Saturation of the red primary; negative desaturates. |
| `GreenHue` | Calibration: Green primary hue | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | Shifts the hue of the camera's green primary; negative is roughly counterclockwise on the colour wheel. Adjust hue first, then saturation. |
| `GreenSaturation` | Calibration: Green primary saturation | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | Saturation of the green primary; negative desaturates. |
| `BlueHue` | Calibration: Blue primary hue | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | Shifts the hue of the camera's blue primary; negative is roughly counterclockwise on the colour wheel. Adjust hue first, then saturation. |
| `BlueSaturation` | Calibration: Blue primary saturation | number | -100 to 100 | 0 | planned | Saturation of the blue primary; negative desaturates. |
